points.description: States that the frequency of light is proportional to its energy (E = hν), so the frequency absorbed determines the energy delivered.
States that the energy levels of an electron bound in an atom are quantized (discrete, only certain allowed values).

Fully explains that for excitation, the photon energy (hence frequency) must exactly equal the energy difference between two allowed levels, so only specific frequencies are absorbed; other frequencies, which match no gap, are not absorbed.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says only certain frequencies match energy gaps but does not clearly say photon energy must equal the level difference (or vice versa).

points.description: States that ejecting an electron (ionization) requires a minimum energy (the ionization energy / threshold), i.e. the electron is free once it is above the highest bound level, where energy is no longer quantized (continuum).
Explains that any photon energy above the threshold is not lost but becomes kinetic energy of the ejected electron, so any frequency above the threshold can be absorbed.

rubric.notes: Equivalent wording earns marks. Full marks need all five ideas: E–frequency link, quantized levels, exact energy-gap matching for excitation, minimum threshold for ejection, and excess energy going to kinetic energy. Answers missing the kinetic-energy explanation lose P5.
